questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating Combinations Given Using Alternate Notation
questions.worked_solution:
First, note that $(\frac{15}{2})$ means the same thing as ${}_{15}{C}_{2}.$

 In general, the number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

Substituting $n=15$ and $r=2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{15}{C}_{2}\text{ } & =\frac{15!}{(15-2)!2!} \\  & =\frac{15!}{13!\cdot 2!} \\  & =\frac{15\cdot 14\cdot \cancel{13!}}{\cancel{13!}\cdot 2!} \\  & =105.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Number of Combinations of Objects Chosen From a Group Fewer Than Ten
questions.problem: Sara has a box of $9$ colored pencils. In how many ways can Sara pick a set of $4$ different pencils from the box?
questions.worked_solution:
The number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

There are $9$ pencils in the box, so $n=9.$ We want to select $4$ of those pencils, so we have $r=4.$

Therefore, the number of different potential sets of four pencils is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{9}{C}_{4} & =\frac{9!}{(9-4)!\,4!} \\  & =\frac{9!}{5!4!} \\  & =\frac{9\cdot 8\cdot 7\cdot 6\cdot \cancel{5!}}{\cancel{5!}4!} \\  & =\frac{9\cdot 8\cdot 7\cdot 6}{4\cdot 3\cdot 2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{3\,024}{24} \\  & =126.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: In a high school, eight players enter trials for the soccer team. In how many ways can the coach select four players to add to the team?
questions.worked_solution:
The number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

There are $8$ players, so $n=8.$ We want to select $4$ of those players for the team, so we have $r=4.$

Therefore, the number of different selections of four players is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{8}{C}_{4} & =\frac{8!}{(8-4)!\,4!} \\  & =\frac{8!}{4!4!} \\  & =\frac{8\cdot 7\cdot 6\cdot 5\cdot \cancel{4!}}{4!\cancel{4!}} \\  & =\frac{1\,680}{24} \\  & =70.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Claire has a bag of candies with $12$ assorted flavors. In how many ways can Claire pick $3$ flavors of candies?
questions.worked_solution:
In general, the number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

There are $12$ flavors, so $n=12.$ We want to select $3$ of those flavors, so we have $r=3.$

Therefore, the number of choices is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{12}{C}_{3} & =\frac{12!}{(12-3)!\,3!} \\  & =\frac{12!}{9!3!} \\  & =\frac{12\cdot 11\cdot 10\cdot \cancel{9!}}{\cancel{9!}3!} \\  & =\frac{12\cdot 11\cdot 10}{3\cdot 2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{1\,320}{6} \\  & =220.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: While Tom was in an elevator within a 100-floor building, it stopped on $5$ different floors. If the order of the floors where the elevator stopped is unimportant, in how many different ways could the elevator stop?
questions.worked_solution:
In general, the number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

There are $100$ floors, so $n=100.$ We want to select $5$ of those floors for the elevator to stop, so we have $r=5.$

Therefore, the number of choices is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{100}{C}_{5} & =\frac{100!}{(100-5)!\,5!} \\  & =\frac{100!}{95!5!} \\  & =\frac{100\cdot 99\cdot 98\cdot 97\cdot 96\cdot \cancel{95!}}{\cancel{95!}5!} \\  & =\frac{100\cdot 99\cdot 98\cdot 97\cdot 96}{5\cdot 4\cdot 3\cdot 2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{9\,034\,502\,400}{120} \\  & =75\,287\,520.\end{aligned}
$$
